static_traits.name: Xu Anmei
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk with, but has not yet shared work-related fears with them; interacts little with colleagues at the new workplace and subjectively feels isolated
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of psychotherapy/psychiatric visits
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to self-reflect and cooperate; emotions mainly anxiety, mentions somatic discomfort of 'my stomach churns at the thought of going to work'

basic_info.main_problem: I feel my new colleagues dislike me and that I will be fired soon.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of isolation and the fear of being fired are affecting my mental health and work performance; I want to feel more connected and safer at work, and to feel better about myself and my work.

core_beliefs: I am not liked / not accepted

special_situations.event: Tries to join colleagues' conversation at lunch but is brushed off
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If what I say is not warmly responded to, it means I am not liked and do not fit in
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Initiates greetings, tries to create topics to gain acceptance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not like me; I am boring

special_situations.event: Finished a project early but no one commented
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not receive recognition and praise from others, it means I did not do well enough / I have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proves himself through harder performance and increased output
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am invisible; I am still not good enough

special_situations.event: His remarks are interrupted or his opinions ignored in team meetings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my views are not adopted, it means they look down on me or do not like me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Prepares and speaks with more effort to prove his ability
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am an outsider; they exclude me

special_situations.event: Sees colleagues chatting harmoniously with each other; the atmosphere changes after he walks into the room
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they do not interact with me, it means they are talking about me/disliking me, and I will be marginalized or even fired
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to join in or win favor through work performance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They definitely do not like me; I might be fired

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted, seen, and recognized, and to build a sense of belonging
core_conflict.fear: Fears rejection, being belittled, and abandonment, and further worries about being fired and losing value
defense_goal: Avoids the blow of 'being rejected' through high self-monitoring and magnifying negative cues
Proving one's worth through doubled effort and output, in exchange for acceptance and a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: An outsider who is not interesting enough and easily overlooked
object_relations.object_representation: A group of colleagues who are indifferent, rejecting, or harshly judgmental
object_relations.linking_affect: Loneliness, shame, anxiety, and a sense of powerlessness

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to recall and weigh positive and negative evidence and focus on positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Positive evidence 'does not carry enough weight / does not count'; it is safer to keep the belief 'they do not like me'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently empathize with their sense of hurt, acknowledge the subjective experience that the positive evidence seems 'weak', and at the same time, in a curious tone, jointly refine the evidence and proportions, without confrontation or excessive persuasion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Talks about situations where the atmosphere changed after entering the room, or colleagues talked among themselves without interacting with them
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets others' silence and busyness as negative views of the self (they are talking about me / dislike me)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Distinguishes 'facts and inferences', asks them to provide evidence and explore other possible explanations; maintains a neutral inquiring tone, avoiding judgment.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about possibly being fired or work performance going unnoticed
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turns disappointment and unease into harsh self-blame and attributions of inadequacy ('I am not good enough / I should not be like this')
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First labels the emotions and needs (being seen / being accepted), then gently externalizes the problem and reduces the intensity of self-blaming language.

manifestations: After starting in a new environment, interaction with colleagues is limited, subjectively experienced as 'being isolated, an outsider'
Seeing colleagues chat warmly with each other while finding it hard to fit in
outcomes: Persistent anxiety and worry about being fired
Interest in daily pleasures such as travel and interacting with the cat declines

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Interpreting colleagues' silence/busyness as 'they hate me, they are talking about me'
A change in atmosphere upon entering a room is interpreted as being directed at oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently self-blames 'I am not interesting enough / not good enough', 'whatever I do is not enough'
When positive feedback appears, still quickly negates its value (believing it 'does not count')

exception_events.target_problem: In the new work environment, Xu Anmei usually feels that colleagues dislike her and that she is excluded, thus feeling strong anxiety and worrying about being fired, with positive interactions rarely occurring.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At a formal presentation, a colleague praised their presentation / expression ability; this time they received positive feedback, different from past experiences of being ignored.
exception_events.reason: Clues: in formal settings, their professional competence was clearly seen and the feedback path was clear, thus more easily triggering positive responses.

exception_events.target_problem: In daily collaboration and informal communication situations, she usually finds it hard to be invited to participate, and consequently feels like an 'outsider'.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few weeks ago, a colleague proactively sought her opinion when a task was blocked; the interaction went smoothly, making her feel needed and recognized.
exception_events.reason: Clues: others proactively sought help with concrete problems, roles and goals were clear, making their professional value more easily seen and affirmed.

positive_force: Possesses solid professional ability and output (able to complete projects ahead of schedule, presentations praised)
A few positive interaction experiences that have occurred (being asked for opinions by colleagues, receiving praise)
Willing to try new methods and maintain a cooperative attitude
Having some foundation of social support (several friends who can be contacted)
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, mind reading, and fortune telling are prominent
Over-relying on external evaluation to define self-worth (external validation)
Self-reproach and negative selective attention, easy to ignore positive evidence
In a new environment, objectively low frequency of interaction reinforces subjective isolation experience
Persistent anxiety and physical discomfort weaken engagement in work and life

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated worry and negative interpretations in work settings ('they hate me / I will be fired'), accompanied by anxiety and stomach discomfort
antecedent: Little interaction with colleagues after starting the new job
Being interrupted or ignored when speaking in team meetings
Seeing colleagues chatting amicably with each other while not being invited to join
target_behavior.core_reason: High need for acceptance and dependence on external validation, accompanied by cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, mind reading, and fortune telling maintaining vigilance
target_behavior.function: Gains a sense of control by anticipating the worst outcome, avoiding uncertainty and the emotional pain of potential rejection
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety rose with somatic discomfort; work performance affected and social engagement further weakened, enjoyment of life declined

target_behavior.behavior: Negates or weakens positive feedback (treating praise and being asked for opinions as 'not weighty enough / not counting')
antecedent: Praised by a colleague for presentation skills
Being proactively asked for an opinion by a colleague
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'I am not good enough / not liked' and confirmation bias are maintained, avoiding conflict with the existing self-schema
target_behavior.function: Maintaining cognitive consistency, lowering expectations to avoid the pain of dashed hopes
target_behavior.consequence: Self-esteem and sense of belonging are hard to repair, persistent feelings of isolation and anxiety are maintained
